Author: Codex-external_model
Date: 2026-10-17 Europe/London (2026-10-16 UTC)
Scope: continuum induction consistency of the prescribed magnetic inner boundary.
No production solver source or production result was modified, and no simulation
was launched by this audit.

FINDING

The daily GONG/WSA-driven radial field is not exactly compatible with the imposed
purely radial velocity and simple Parker-spiral tangential field. On source days
22 through31, corresponding to2025-11-23 inclusive through2025-12-03 exclusive,
the radial Faraday residual RMS divided by Br RMS is0.2511day^-1 within±30degrees,
and0.2665day^-1 within±60degrees when source_surface_au=0. These are substantial
boundary driving incompatibilities, not measured solar nonideal electric fields
and not percentages of numerical divergence. They include coronal-model changes,
synoptic updates and regridding, rather than representing only true solar evolution.

The proposed extra rotation mismatch for source_surface_au=.01AU has the sign
suggested by root. However, the CURRENT inspected mainC++source uses the default
source_surface_au=0, and no archivedcfg/python/json file sets a nonzero value.
The inspected mediumrun.cfg omits it. Thus.01AU is a hypothetical sensitivity case,
not an established explanation of the production results. Historical binary/config
provenance would be needed to make a stronger claim about earlier runs.

With.01AU, rotation alone contributes roughly0.11day^-1 normalized RMS and the
combined residual rises to0.2708day^-1 at±30degrees and0.2842day^-1 at±60degrees.
Setting the source radius to zero fixes a frozen Carrington pattern's rotation
consistency, but does not fix the actual daily map changes.

DERIVATION AND SIGN

Use standard spherical coordinates(r,theta,lambda), with theta colatitude and
lambda increasing in the direction of solar rotation. The solver's fixed inertial
solar-equatorial longitude islambda, and Carrington map longitude is
  phi=lambda−Omega*t−phase.
Write the prescribed field at the shell as
  Br(t,theta,lambda)=q(t,theta,phi).
The boundary imposes vtheta=vphi=Btheta=0 and
  Bphi=−Omega*(r−rss)*sin(theta)*Br/vr.
Ideal MHD gives E=−v×B, hence
  Etheta=vr*Bphi=−Omega*(r−rss)*sin(theta)*Br,
  Ephi=0.
The radial component of Faraday's law is
  partial_t Br=−(curl E)_r
              =+[1/(r sin(theta))]*partial_lambda Etheta
              =−Omega*(1−rss/r)*partial_phi q.
But the actual prescribed time derivative at fixed inertial longitude is
  partial_t Br=partial_t q−Omega*partial_phi q.
Thus the continuum mismatch, with the residual defined as the left side of
Faraday's law, is
  R := partial_t Br+(curl E)_r
     = partial_t q−Omega*(rss/r)*partial_phi q.
The minus sign in the rotation correction is therefore confirmed. No dependence
on the scalar boundary speed survives because vr cancels out of Etheta. This
cancellation remains true when daily speed, density and temperature evolve.

DATA AND QUANTITATIVE METHOD

The audit reads the ACTUAL calibrated inputs/boundary_map.csv and its metadata,
not an invented analytic map or an older raw-field normalization. Source SHA256
is in summary.json. There are25maps,90south-to-north latitudes and180longitudes.
The radius is0.0999850461AU andOmega0.2475644824rad/day.

The imposed boundary uses linear time interpolation and periodic linear longitude
interpolation. At each longitude segment midpoint, q is the average of its two
endpoints and partial_phi q is exactly their forward difference divided by the
2degree spacing. Time derivatives are exactly the inter-map slopes. The squared
residual and squared field are integrated analytically in time, including clipped
window endpoints. Latitude averages usecos(latitude), proportional to exact areas
of the uniform2degree latitude cells. The aggregate is sqrt(integral R² / integral
q²), with the same area/time measure in both integrals. It is not an unweighted
average of ratios near Br=0. All statistics describe this source-grid boundary
interpolant; production-grid smoothing can change the sampled gradients.

                     ±30degrees          ±60degrees
Br RMS[nT]             366.336              365.716
RMS(dq/dt)[nT/day]      91.992               97.462
RMS(dq/dt)/BrRMS        0.251113             0.266497day^-1
Rotation only,.01AU     0.112300             0.110923day^-1
Combined R,.01AU        0.270808             0.284193day^-1
Corr(dq/dt,dq/dphi)     0.04134              0.04328

The two terms are almost uncorrelated, so they add approximately in quadrature
for this descriptive RMS. This is a numerical identity for the source fields,
not a probabilistic uncertainty model. Individual interval normalized residuals
forrss=0range0.0748--0.5141day^-1 in±30degrees and0.0909--0.4882 in±60degrees.
Detailed intervals and source times are in interval_metrics.csv/.json.

The global surface-mean field is small but not identically zero. Across available
maps, max|meanBr|/BrRMS is0.001117(0.112%). In the tested window, the surface-mean
time derivative RMS is0.3367nT/day, much smaller than the total95.57nT/day full-
sphere map-evolution RMS. A globally smooth tangential electric field cannot change
total radial magnetic flux: the l=0 part must be made time-independent or removed
before solving for a global inductive correction. This is a small monopole issue
in amplitude, but an exact solvability requirement.

CONTROLLED SMALL DIAGNOSTIC INPUT

boundary_map_Br_frozen_day26.csv is ready for an optional comparison run. It keeps
all source times, coordinates, daily speed, density and temperature numerically
identical to inputs/boundary_map.csv; ONLY the Carrington Br pattern is held fixed.
The pattern is interpolated to day26=2025-11-27T00:00UTC from observed-driven maps
at days25.0097 and26.0097, using fraction0.9903. The compact frozen_Br_day26.npz
also stores this one actual pattern and coordinates. This is a corotating frozen
magnetic pattern, not a field frozen in inertial space, and is an explicit diagnostic
scenario rather than a replacement observation product.

For this frozen pattern andrss=0, R is analytically zero at the continuum boundary.
Withrss=.01, the same frozen pattern retains normalized residual0.14904day^-1
within±30degrees and0.14818 within±60degrees. Thus freezing alone would not fix a
nonzero-source-radius rotation mismatch. Use identical numerical method/domain
and source radius for the evolving-vs-frozen comparison. Quantify field divergence
and comet density/flux response separately; the induction audit alone does not
predict how much the density estimate will change.

Reproduce metrics using:
  python external_model/induction_audit/audit_induction.py
Create/recreate the optional table using:
  python external_model/induction_audit/audit_induction.py --write-frozen-table
The source calibrated table and numpy/astropy are required; no network or new
library installation is used. The table is about31MB, while the compressed single
frozen pattern is about116kB. Non-Br-column equality and fixed-Br checks passed.

POSSIBLE INDUCTIVE EMF CORRECTION

For an evolving boundary, a full-sphere surface-Poisson construction is available
once the global l=0 residual is removed. Seek a tangential correction
  delta E=(er cross grad_surface Psi),
where grad_surface is the physical gradient on the radiusr0sphere. Components are
  delta Etheta=−partial_phi Psi/(r0 sin(theta)),
  delta Ephi=+partial_theta Psi/r0.
Then
  (curl delta E)_r=(Delta_unit_sphere Psi)/r0².
Choose
  Delta_unit_sphere Psi=−r0²R.
For spherical harmonicsl>=1 this is
  Psi_lm=r0² R_lm/[l(l+1)].
This is the minimum-norm solenoidal tangential-EMF part; an arbitrary surface-gradient
electric field can still be added without changing radial Faraday evolution.
On the available full-sphere maps the correction is computationally modest. A
wedge-only Poisson problem would introduce additional arbitrary latitude-edge
conditions, so full-sphere reconstruction is preferable.

If retaining purely radial velocity and ideal E=−v×B, one can represent that EMF
through corrected tangential magnetic fields:
  delta Bphi=delta Etheta/vr,
  delta Btheta=−delta Ephi/vr.
This changes magnetic stresses/energy and is a modelling choice: the original WSA
maps do not independently observe those tangential components. It should not be
introduced as an invisible numerical repair. It needs unit-consistent implementation,
polar treatment, convergence checks and a quantitative correction-amplitude audit.
No such correction was silently added here.

LIMITS: INITIAL FIELD AND CAUSATION

Boundary compatibility is not the whole divergence problem. initial() retards the
maps using a lag based on the reference400km/s while its Parker Bphi divides by
local angularly varying speed. Even with a frozen map andrss=0, that generic
retarded radialBr and local-speedBphi are not guaranteed to form a divergence-free
3D initial field. Exact cancellation occurs only in special consistent radial-flow
cases. Daily time evolution adds further initial incompatibility. A vector-potential
or CT-consistent field initialization would address a different part of the problem.

Interior discretization, GLM flux/damping, time-varying cleaning speed and latitude
boundary conditions can also contribute. The present nonzero R demonstrates an
inconsistent set of prescribed continuum boundary variables; it does not prove
that this is the dominant cause of the observed numerical divergence or quantify
the density/flux bias. A matched frozen-boundary experiment with adequate spinup
is a useful discriminator, with initial-field and method effects still disclosed.
